facts.text: Budget: reportedly $550, and most of it went to feeding the cast and a wrap party. Director Dave Wascavage financed it himself, with no outside investors.
Dave Wascavage wrote, directed, shot, edited, scored and did the sound and effects. He also played several roles, including Dave the Fisherman and a Waiter.
Those Sasquatch growls are the director himself. He growled into a microphone and dropped the pitch, and it reportedly took about three minutes.
Wascavage's wife Mary co-wrote the film and caught the crew, and his mother Loretta plays Rick's mom. His father and brother also appear.
Night is expensive, so the whole movie was shot in daylight. That's why the "night" scenes look so sunny.
The Sasquatch suit was homemade. Its baggy look came from the budget and from the director never having built a costume before.
On the CGI: "I literally just learned it that day or the day before." Wascavage taught himself the effects as he went.
The newspaper "office" is Henderson High School in West Chester, PA. Look out the windows for football practice.
Juan Fernandez (Steve) was cast in a small role. He impressed so much in his audition that he was bumped up to a lead.
The film took about 1.5 years of shooting, editing and post-production. It was about 3 years from first script draft to distribution deal.
Some CG shots were added in editing because reshooting live action wasn't possible in winter conditions.
Neil Hope, Wheels on Degrassi, has an uncredited cameo. It was reportedly his last role.
Talia's costume came from a mall trip. Wascavage took actress Sue Lynn Sanchez shopping for boots and fringed clothing.
Sue Lynn Sanchez, who plays Talia, is also a spokes-model for Fiji Water.
Red Letter Media made it a Best of the Worst pick in November 2017. Jay Bauman called it "so bad, so stupid, and so charming."
Wascavage on critics: personal attacks say "less about me and more about what they expect." He stayed unfazed by the bad reviews.
TMDB lists the budget at $12,000. Other sources say $550. Either way, it's a lot of Sasquatch for the money.
Wascavage's songs are in the film. "Trust In Thee" is performed by his mother Loretta, and "Collision Force" by his wife Mary.
Dave Bonavita and Wes Miller also appeared in Wascavage's earlier no-budget film Fungicide (2002).
The Visual Vengeance Blu-ray has a director commentary, a CGI featurette and behind-the-scenes footage. It also has a RiffTrax version.
Wascavage says Suburban Sasquatch 2 and 3 are written and ready to go, along with Fungicide 2.
The film gets name-checked in other cult movie fare, including Lycan Colony, RiffTrax's Avengers: Endgame and The American Scream.
The crazy credits include one line: "Bigfoot is real."
